classification.difficultyReason: The composition requires splitting an inner-function branch at a new breakpoint, then graphing three restricted pieces with distinct open and closed endpoints.

answer.short:
$$f(g(x))=\begin{cases}(x+2)^2&x<-2\\-x-1&-2\le x<1\\1-x&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

Split the $x<1$ branch at $x=-2$, where $g(x)=0$.
answer.worked:
For $x<1$, $g(x)=x+2$. Its sign changes at $x=-2$.

For $x<-2$, $g(x)<0$, so use the square branch of $f$:
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=(x+2)^2.\end{align*}$$

For $-2\le x<1$, $g(x)\ge0$, so
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=1-(x+2)\\f(g(x))&=-x-1.\end{align*}$$

For $x\ge1$, $g(x)=x\ge0$, so
$$\begin{align*}f(g(x))&=1-x.\end{align*}$$

Therefore,
$$f(g(x))=\begin{cases}(x+2)^2&x<-2\\-x-1&-2\le x<1\\1-x&x\ge1.\end{cases}$$

answer.short:
Open endpoints: $(-2,0)$ and $(1,-2)$. Closed endpoints: $(-2,1)$ and $(1,0)$.

Plot each branch only on its stated interval, as shown.
answer.worked:
For $x<-2$, draw the left-hand branch of $y=(x+2)^2$, with an open endpoint at $(-2,0)$.

For $-2\le x<1$, draw the segment of $y=-x-1$ from the closed endpoint $(-2,1)$ to the open endpoint $(1,-2)$.

For $x\ge1$, draw the ray $y=1-x$ from the closed endpoint $(1,0)$ towards the lower right. This ray passes through $(2,-1)$.
